The name evokes images of radiance, illumination, and the start of new beginnings.

During a raid by the invading Cumans, Svetlana was taken captive and held in a pagan temple. There, she converted her captor, who later became known as Prince Igor Sviatoslavich of Novgorod. This marked the beginning of a significant period of Christianization in Novgorod.

In this work, Svetlana is the name of a noblewoman, born around 1796, who is married to Count Pierre Bezukhov. She is a gentle, pious, and intelligent woman, and is beloved by many in the novel, including Pierre and Andrei Bolkonsky. Despite her virtues, Svetlana's life is marked by tragedy, including the death of her husband and her own untimely demise.
